# Predictor Exploration

Our goal is to identify predictors that improve national
championship forecasts beyond overall team strength.

We use historical seasons through 2021 for exploration and
reserve 2022–2026 for final model evaluation.

The current dataset contains pre-Selection Sunday statistics.
Results are provisional until we construct comparable December
snapshots.

## 1. Load and Prepare Data

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from sklearn.model_selection import GroupKFold
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import (
    log_loss,
    average_precision_score,
    brier_score_loss
)

# Find the v2 dataset
paths = [
    Path("data/processed/champion_checklist_v2.csv"),
    Path("../data/processed/champion_checklist_v2.csv")
]

data_path = next((p for p in paths if p.exists()), None)

if data_path is None:
    raise FileNotFoundError("Could not find the v2 dataset.")

data = pd.read_csv(data_path)

# Keep all eligible D1 teams
teams = data.loc[
    ~data["is_reclassifying"].fillna(False)
].copy()

teams["champion_label"] = (
    teams["champion"].eq(True)
).astype(int)

# Only historical development seasons
train = teams.loc[
    teams["season"] <= 2021
].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

cv = GroupKFold(n_splits=5)

print("Training teams:", len(train))
print("Training champions:", train["champion_label"].sum())
print("Training seasons:", train["season"].nunique())
```

## Compare the predictor combos

```{python}

# Candidate predictors grouped by basketball relevance

base = ["adj_em", "wab_z", "sos_rank"]

candidate_models = {
    "AdjEM only": ["adj_em"],

    "Strength + resume": base,

    "Offense + defense": ["adj_o", "adj_d"],

    "Offense + defense + resume": [
        "adj_o", "adj_d", "wab_z", "sos_rank"
    ],

    "Add eFG margin":
        base + ["adj_efg_margin"],

    "Add turnover edge":
        base + ["adj_tov_edge"],

    "Add rebounding edge":
        base + ["adj_reb_edge"],

    "Add FT rate margin":
        base + ["adj_ftr_margin"],

    "Add 3PT percentage":
        base + ["three_pt_pct"],

    "Add FT percentage":
        base + ["ft_pct"],

    "Add 3PT attempt rate":
        base + ["three_par"],

    "Add recent wins":
        base + ["last10_wins"],

    "Add recent scoring margin":
        base + ["last10_avg_margin"],

    "Add four factors": base + [
        "adj_efg_margin",
        "adj_tov_edge",
        "adj_reb_edge",
        "adj_ftr_margin"
    ],

    "Add shooting + form": base + [
        "three_pt_pct", "ft_pct", "last10_wins"
    ],

    "Expanded model": base + [
        "adj_efg_margin",
        "adj_tov_edge",
        "adj_reb_edge",
        "adj_ftr_margin",
        "three_pt_pct",
        "ft_pct",
        "three_par",
        "last10_wins",
        "last10_avg_margin",
        "adj_tempo"
    ]
}

results = []

for name, predictors in candidate_models.items():

    X = train[predictors]
    y = train["champion_label"]

    assert X.notna().all().all(), name

    probabilities = np.zeros(len(train))

    # Hold entire seasons out during validation
    for fit_idx, valid_idx in cv.split(
        X, y, groups=train["season"]
    ):

        model = make_pipeline(
            StandardScaler(),
            LogisticRegression(
                penalty="l2",
                C=1.0,
                max_iter=5000
            )
        )

        model.fit(
            X.iloc[fit_idx],
            y.iloc[fit_idx]
        )

        probabilities[valid_idx] = (
            model.predict_proba(
                X.iloc[valid_idx]
            )[:, 1]
        )

    # Rank teams within each season
    ranked = train[
        ["season", "team", "champion_label"]
    ].copy()

    ranked["probability"] = probabilities

    ranked["rank"] = ranked.groupby(
        "season"
    )["probability"].rank(
        ascending=False,
        method="min"
    )

    champions = ranked.loc[
        ranked["champion_label"] == 1
    ]

    results.append({
        "Model": name,
        "Predictors": len(predictors),
        "Log Loss": log_loss(y, probabilities),
        "Avg Precision": average_precision_score(
            y, probabilities
        ),
        "Brier Score": brier_score_loss(
            y, probabilities
        ),
        "Top 5": int(
            (champions["rank"] <= 5).sum()
        ),
        "Top 10": int(
            (champions["rank"] <= 10).sum()
        ),
        "Mean Champion Rank":
            champions["rank"].mean()
    })

performance = pd.DataFrame(results).sort_values(
    "Log Loss"
)

print("PREDICTOR COMPARISON — V2")
print(performance.round(5).to_string(index=False))
```

## Note: NIL-Era Model Validity

Our original model uses seasons 2005–2021 for training and 2022–2026 for testing. Since NCAA NIL rules took effect in July 2021, this division also separates the pre-NIL and NIL eras.

This creates a potential distribution shift: relationships learned from historical college basketball may not completely represent modern roster construction and team performance.

We investigated this by comparing an identical model across pre-NIL and NIL-era evaluation periods. Performance declined slightly in the NIL era, but the model still ranked all five modern champions in its top ten.

We also tested walk-forward validation, adding completed NIL-era seasons to the training data as they became available. Results were nearly identical to the model trained only through 2021.

These findings do not establish that NIL has or has not changed championship prediction. For now, we will retain the full historical dataset, test modern-era performance separately, and investigate whether roster-related predictors provide additional value. We will revisit this analysis with the expanded roster data in version 3.

## Roster Continuity and Experience

```{python}

# Roster exploration: use training seasons with v2 roster data
roster_train = train.loc[

base_features = ["adj_em", "wab_z", "sos_rank"]

roster_candidates = {
    "Strength + resume": base_features,
    "Add returner minutes":
        base_features + ["ret_same_min_pct"],
    "Add returner points":
        base_features + ["ret_same_pts_pct"],

print("ROSTER DATA COVERAGE")

print("\nRoster data quality:")

# One season per validation fold
roster_cv = GroupKFold(n_splits=5)
roster_results = []

for name, features in roster_candidates.items():

    X = roster_train[features]

        probabilities[valid_idx] = (
            model.predict_proba(
                X.iloc[valid_idx]
            )[:, 1]
        )

    ranked = roster_train[
        ["season", "team", "champion_label"]
    ].copy()

    ranked["probability"] = probabilities
    ranked["rank"] = ranked.groupby(
        "season"
    )["probability"].rank(
        ascending=False,
        method="min"

    champions = ranked.loc[
        ranked["champion_label"] == 1

        "Model": name,
        "Log Loss": log_loss(y, probabilities),

        "Top 10": int(
            (champions["rank"] <= 10).sum()

roster_performance = pd.DataFrame(
    roster_results
).sort_values("Log Loss")

print("\nROSTER PREDICTOR COMPARISON")
print(
    roster_performance.round(5).to_string(index=False)
)
```

## Roster Predictor Stability

```{python}

# Evaluate roster predictors across alternative samples.
# Only historical training seasons are used.

def roster_oof(frame, features):
    frame = frame.reset_index(drop=True)
    X = frame[features]
    y = frame["champion_label"]

    cv = GroupKFold(
        n_splits=frame["season"].nunique()
    )

    probabilities = np.zeros(len(frame))

    for train_idx, valid_idx in cv.split(
        X, y, groups=frame["season"]
    ):
        model = make_pipeline(
            StandardScaler(),
            LogisticRegression(
                C=1.0,
                max_iter=5000
            )
        )

        model.fit(
            X.iloc[train_idx],
            y.iloc[train_idx]
        )

        probabilities[valid_idx] = (
            model.predict_proba(
                X.iloc[valid_idx]
            )[:, 1]
        )

    return probabilities


samples = {
    "All roster seasons": roster_train,
    "High-quality rosters": roster_train[
        roster_train["roster_quality"] == "ok"
    ],
    "Exclude 2016": roster_train[
        roster_train["season"] != 2016
    ]
}

models_to_check = {
    "Strength + resume": base_features,
    "Add returner points":
        base_features + ["ret_same_pts_pct"],
    "Add returner minutes":
        base_features + ["ret_same_min_pct"]
}

stability_rows = []

for sample_name, frame in samples.items():
    frame = frame.reset_index(drop=True)

    for model_name, features in models_to_check.items():
        probs = roster_oof(frame, features)

        ranked = frame[
            ["season", "champion_label"]
        ].copy()

        ranked["probability"] = probs
        ranked["rank"] = ranked.groupby(
            "season"
        )["probability"].rank(
            ascending=False, method="min"
        )

        champions = ranked[
            ranked["champion_label"] == 1
        ]

        stability_rows.append({
            "Sample": sample_name,
            "Model": model_name,
            "Teams": len(frame),
            "Champions": int(
                frame["champion_label"].sum()
            ),
            "Log Loss": log_loss(
                frame["champion_label"], probs
            ),
            "Top 5": int(
                (champions["rank"] <= 5).sum()
            )
        })

stability_results = pd.DataFrame(stability_rows)

print(
    stability_results.round(5).to_string(index=False)
)
```

## Pre-NIL vs. NIL-Only vs. Full-History Training

```{python}

# Compare historical training strategies on 2026.
# The 2026 season is NEVER included in training.

from sklearn.metrics import log_loss, brier_score_loss

features = ["adj_em", "wab_z", "sos_rank"]

train_periods = {
    "Pre-NIL (2005-2021)":
        teams["season"] <= 2021,

    "NIL-only (2022-2025)":
        teams["season"].between(2022, 2025),

    "Full history (2005-2025)":
        teams["season"] <= 2025
}

test_2026 = teams.loc[
    teams["season"] == 2026
].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

assert test_2026["champion_label"].sum() == 1

results_2026 = []

for name, mask in train_periods.items():

    training = teams.loc[mask].copy()

    model = make_pipeline(
        StandardScaler(),
        LogisticRegression(
            C=1.0,
            solver="lbfgs",
            max_iter=5000
        )
    )

    model.fit(
        training[features],
        training["champion_label"]
    )

    probabilities = model.predict_proba(
        test_2026[features]
    )[:, 1]

    ranked = test_2026[
        ["team", "champion_label"]
    ].copy()

    ranked["score"] = probabilities
    ranked["rank"] = ranked["score"].rank(
        ascending=False,
        method="min"
    )

    champion = ranked.loc[
        ranked["champion_label"] == 1
    ].iloc[0]

    results_2026.append({
        "Training Period": name,
        "Training Teams": len(training),
        "Training Champions": int(
            training["champion_label"].sum()
        ),
        "Champion Rank": int(champion["rank"]),
        "Log Loss": log_loss(
            test_2026["champion_label"],
            probabilities
        ),
        "Brier Score": brier_score_loss(
            test_2026["champion_label"],
            probabilities
        ),
        "Top 5": ", ".join(
            ranked.nlargest(5, "score")["team"]
        )
    })

era_results = pd.DataFrame(results_2026)

print("2026 CHAMPIONSHIP MODEL COMPARISON")
print(era_results.round(5).to_string(index=False))
```

## NIL-Era Walk-Forward Validation

```{python}

# Compare training strategies across 2024-2026.
# All predictions use only prior completed seasons.

features = ["adj_em", "wab_z", "sos_rank"]

walkforward_rows = []

for test_year in [2024, 2025, 2026]:

    test_year_data = teams.loc[
        teams["season"] == test_year
    ].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

    strategies = {
        "Pre-NIL": teams["season"] <= 2021,

        "NIL-only": teams["season"].between(
            2022, test_year - 1
        ),

        "Full history": teams["season"] < test_year
    }

    for name, mask in strategies.items():

        training = teams.loc[mask].copy()

        model = make_pipeline(
            StandardScaler(),
            LogisticRegression(
                C=1.0,
                solver="lbfgs",
                max_iter=5000
            )
        )

        model.fit(
            training[features],
            training["champion_label"]
        )

        probs = model.predict_proba(
            test_year_data[features]
        )[:, 1]

        ranked = test_year_data[
            ["team", "champion_label"]
        ].copy()

        ranked["probability"] = probs
        ranked["rank"] = ranked["probability"].rank(
            ascending=False,
            method="min"
        )

        champion = ranked.loc[
            ranked["champion_label"] == 1
        ].iloc[0]

        walkforward_rows.append({
            "Season": test_year,
            "Training": name,
            "Train Champions": int(
                training["champion_label"].sum()
            ),
            "Champion Rank": int(champion["rank"]),
            "Log Loss": log_loss(
                test_year_data["champion_label"],
                probs
            ),
            "Brier": brier_score_loss(
                test_year_data["champion_label"],
                probs
            ),
            "Top 5 Hit": int(champion["rank"] <= 5)
        })

walkforward = pd.DataFrame(walkforward_rows)

print("WALK-FORWARD RESULTS")
print(walkforward.round(5).to_string(index=False))

# Compare average performance across all three seasons
summary = walkforward.groupby("Training").agg(
    Avg_Log_Loss=("Log Loss", "mean"),
    Avg_Brier=("Brier", "mean"),
    Avg_Champion_Rank=("Champion Rank", "mean"),
    Top_5_Hits=("Top 5 Hit", "sum")
).sort_values("Avg_Log_Loss")

print("\nTHREE-SEASON SUMMARY")
print(summary.round(5).to_string())
```

## Does weighting recent seasons improve predictions?

```{python}

# Compare equal-weight and recent-weighted training.
# Each test season is excluded from its training data.

features = ["adj_em", "wab_z", "sos_rank"]

weighting_strategies = {
    "Full history": None,
    "10-year half-life": 10,
    "5-year half-life": 5
}

weighted_results = []

for test_year in [2024, 2025, 2026]:

    historical = teams.loc[
        teams["season"] < test_year
    ].copy()

    test_data = teams.loc[
        teams["season"] == test_year
    ].copy()

    for name, half_life in weighting_strategies.items():

        # Most recent completed season has weight 1
        ages = (
            test_year - 1 - historical["season"].to_numpy()
        )

        if half_life is None:
            weights = np.ones(len(historical))
        else:
            weights = 0.5 ** (ages / half_life)

        # Normalize mean weight so regularization strength
        # remains comparable across strategies.
        weights = weights / weights.mean()

        model = make_pipeline(
            StandardScaler(),
            LogisticRegression(
                penalty="l2",
                C=1.0,
                max_iter=5000
            )
        )

        model.fit(
            historical[features],
            historical["champion_label"],
            standardscaler__sample_weight=weights,
            logisticregression__sample_weight=weights
        )

        probs = model.predict_proba(
            test_data[features]
        )[:, 1]

        actual = test_data["champion_label"].to_numpy()

        # Convert team-level odds into a within-season
        # distribution that sums to 1.
        clipped = np.clip(probs, 1e-12, 1 - 1e-12)
        odds = clipped / (1 - clipped)
        season_probs = odds / odds.sum()

        champion_idx = np.flatnonzero(actual == 1)
        assert len(champion_idx) == 1

        champ_idx = champion_idx[0]
        champion_probability = season_probs[champ_idx]

        ranked = pd.Series(probs).rank(
            ascending=False,
            method="min"
        )

        weighted_results.append({
            "Season": test_year,
            "Model": name,
            "Log Loss": log_loss(actual, probs),
            "Brier": brier_score_loss(actual, probs),
            "Champion Rank": int(ranked.iloc[champ_idx]),
            "Top 5": int(ranked.iloc[champ_idx] <= 5),
            "Champion Share": champion_probability,
            "Winner Log Score": -np.log(
                champion_probability
            )
        })

weighted_comparison = pd.DataFrame(weighted_results)

print("RECENCY-WEIGHTED MODEL COMPARISON")
print(
    weighted_comparison.round(5).to_string(index=False)
)

weighted_summary = weighted_comparison.groupby(
    "Model"
).agg(
    Avg_Log_Loss=("Log Loss", "mean"),
    Avg_Brier=("Brier", "mean"),
    Avg_Winner_Log_Score=("Winner Log Score", "mean"),
    Avg_Champion_Rank=("Champion Rank", "mean"),
    Top_5_Hits=("Top 5", "sum")
).sort_values("Avg_Winner_Log_Score")

print("\nRECENCY-WEIGHTED SUMMARY")
print(weighted_summary.round(5).to_string())
```

## Provisional Model Comparison

```{python}

# Compare our leading feature sets and weighting strategies.
# Retrospective evaluation: these seasons have already been
# examined during exploratory model development.

feature_sets = {
    "Core 3": ["adj_em", "wab_z", "sos_rank"],
    "Core 3 + FT%": [
        "adj_em", "wab_z", "sos_rank", "ft_pct"
    ]
}

weighting_options = {
    "Equal": None,
    "5-year half-life": 5
}

provisional_results = []

for test_year in range(2022, 2027):

    historical = teams.loc[
        teams["season"] < test_year
    ].copy()

    future = teams.loc[
        teams["season"] == test_year
    ].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

    actual = future["champion_label"].to_numpy()

    assert actual.sum() == 1

    for feature_name, features in feature_sets.items():

        for weight_name, half_life in weighting_options.items():

            ages = (
                test_year - 1 -
                historical["season"].to_numpy()
            )

            if half_life is None:
                weights = np.ones(len(historical))
            else:
                weights = 0.5 ** (ages / half_life)

            weights = weights / weights.mean()

            model = make_pipeline(
                StandardScaler(),
                LogisticRegression(
                    penalty="l2",
                    C=1.0,
                    max_iter=5000
                )
            )

            model.fit(
                historical[features],
                historical["champion_label"],
                standardscaler__sample_weight=weights,
                logisticregression__sample_weight=weights
            )

            probs = model.predict_proba(
                future[features]
            )[:, 1]

            ranks = pd.Series(probs).rank(
                ascending=False,
                method="min"
            )

            winner_index = np.flatnonzero(actual == 1)[0]
            winner_rank = int(ranks.iloc[winner_index])

            provisional_results.append({
                "Season": test_year,
                "Features": feature_name,
                "Weighting": weight_name,
                "Log Loss": log_loss(actual, probs),
                "Brier": brier_score_loss(actual, probs),
                "Champion Rank": winner_rank,
                "Top 5 Hit": int(winner_rank <= 5)
            })

provisional = pd.DataFrame(provisional_results)

summary = provisional.groupby(
    ["Features", "Weighting"]
).agg(
    Avg_Log_Loss=("Log Loss", "mean"),
    Avg_Brier=("Brier", "mean"),
    Avg_Champion_Rank=("Champion Rank", "mean"),
    Top_5_Hits=("Top 5 Hit", "sum")
).sort_values("Avg_Log_Loss")

print("FIVE-SEASON MODEL COMPARISON")
print(summary.round(5).to_string())

print("\nYEAR-BY-YEAR RESULTS")
print(
    provisional.round(5).to_string(index=False)
)
```

## Analysis Conclusions (for now)

Our exploratory analysis compared multiple predictor combinations, roster statistics, and historical training strategies to identify a provisional model for predicting NCAA national champions.

Overall, adjusted efficiency margin, Wins Above Bubble, and strength-of-schedule rank provided the most consistent starting point. Adding additional basketball statistics occasionally improved individual seasons, but did not consistently improve overall predictive performance.

We also tested whether NIL-era training or additional weighting of recent seasons improved predictions. While the five-year recency-weighted model achieved slightly lower average log loss, its improvement was small and did not increase our top-five champion identification rate.

Roster continuity showed promising results, particularly the percentage of team points scored by returning players. However, version 2 only provides five historical training champions with roster data, limiting how confidently we can evaluate these relationships.

For now, we selected a three-predictor ridge logistic regression model trained on the full historical dataset with equal weights as our provisional baseline.

Future work: Reevaluate roster continuity, transfer participation, and player experience using the expanded historical coverage in version 3. We will also investigate early-season data availability, probability calibration, and whether modern-era weighting improves predictions when roster variables are included.

These findings are exploratory because several model choices were evaluated against the same recent seasons. Additional independent validation will be necessary before claiming reliable future-season performance.
